subject: Helio Retail: intermittent slow responses on live chat (streaming)
message_1_subject: Helio Retail: intermittent slow responses on live chat (streaming)
message_1_body:
Hi team,

We started seeing spikes in user-visible latency on our live help widget around 13:45 PST today. The UI shows the typing indicator for 3–8 seconds before any tokens arrive; this is noticeable across browsers and regions. We collect some telemetry and attached a CSV export of a few representative requests (helio-telemetry-extract-20281108.csv).

Impact: about 1.2% of sessions in the last 30m have >2s initial token latency; downstream UI times out on a subset. This is hitting our peak shopping hours; engineering and product are watching.

Can you confirm whether this is a regional edge issue, runtime backlog, or something on our config? Any immediate mitigations we can apply while you investigate?

Thanks,
Asha Menon
Director, Product Operations
Helio Retail

Attachments: helio-telemetry-extract-20281108.csv
message_2_subject: Re: Helio Retail: intermittent slow responses on live chat (streaming)
message_2_body:
Hi Asha — thanks for the heads up and for the telemetry. We see the traces you attached and are triaging with infra and runtime. Initial notes:

- Pattern looks like occasional kernel-level queueing on a subset of host pools servicing the us-west region.
- We're not seeing broad model-level degradation (token emit times from the model container are nominal) which points to proxy/edge or kernel batch spikes.

Short-term actions we can apply right away (we can flip these for you if you want us to):
1) Route Helio traffic to alternative edge pool in us-east for a portion of traffic (can be done as a gradual split to avoid cache cold-starts).
2) Apply a temporary client-side fallback: lower max_tokens_per_stream to 512 and enforce a 30s client-side heartbeat to avoid UI stalls.
3) Enable a conservative batching profile (temp-config-suggestions-v1.pdf) that reduces queueing for low-latency sessions.

If you authorize, I can kick off a split to us-east and push the temp batching profile now and monitor. We'll keep you posted with telemetry and a follow-up postmortem.

— Soojin
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0199

message_3_subject: Re: Helio Retail: intermittent slow responses on live chat (streaming)
message_3_body:
Asha — quick note from the support side while infra applies the changes:

We can implement the following client-safe mitigations immediately on your plan side (no SDK update required):
- Toggle 'edge-fallback' to us-east for 20% of traffic (we can ramp to 50% after 30m if metrics look good).
- Shorten client streaming timeout to 18s to avoid UI showing stuck states; treat timeouts as a soft retry with exponential backoff.

If you'd prefer us to perform the config flips directly, say the word and we'll do a staged rollout. Either way, we'll coordinate a scheduled window for any changes that touch routing.

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

message_4_subject: Helio: mitigation applied and follow-up postmortem link
message_4_body:
Hi Asha — quick update and follow-up from our side: we applied a 25% traffic split to the us-east edge pool and deployed the conservative batching profile last night at 23:10 PST. Observations:

- Initial-token latency for your monitored sessions dropped from a 95th percentile of 1.9s to 0.42s during the 03:00–08:00 monitoring window.
- No errors were introduced by the change; we observed a small increase in cold-cache misses (expected) but no impact to correctness.

We also dropped a short postmortem with technical findings and recommended next steps for a durable fix: https://drive.redwood.com/incident/helio-20281109-postmortem (linked). Highlights: host-pool kernel batching spikes caused transient queueing; engineering will schedule a kernel tuning release and an edge routing policy that keeps low-latency sessions on hot paths.

Next steps for Helio (recommended):
- If you want us to roll the us-east split back to 0% during a low-traffic window after the kernel tuning lands, we can coordinate timelines.
- We recommend keeping the conservative batching profile for two more production days and then re-evaluating.
- We'll share telemetry dashboards and a runbook for client timeouts and heartbeat settings by EOD.

Attached: postmortem-helio-20281109.md and temp-config-suggestions-v1.pdf for your engineering review.

If you want a short sync with infra/ops to walk through the postmortem, suggest a couple of times and we'll get people on the call. Appreciate the quick signal from your team — that made targeted mitigation possible.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
CC: Ben Carter (AE), Karthik Iyer (Solutions)
